newsitem.title: UK: RUGBY UNION-STRANSKY MASTERMINDS TWICKENHAM TRIUMPH.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-STRANSKY MASTERMINDS TWICKENHAM TRIUMPH.

text.p: Former Springbok fly-half Joel Stransky added an English cup winners medal to his impressive collection of rugby honours on Saturday by kicking Leicester to a 9-3 victory over Sale at Twickenham.

Stransky, whose boot was ultimately responsible for South Africa's triumph over New Zealand in the 1995 World Cup, scored all of his side's points to engineer a narrow win over opponents who included former All Blacks Simon Mannix and John Mitchell.

The 29-year-old Stransky's all-round vision and tactical sense were equally crucial factors in a Pilkington Cup final affected by wet and windy conditions, although he was astray with four other penalty attempts.
It was a welcome success for Leicester who were well beaten by French club Brive in the European Cup final in January and faded from contention in the league towards the end of a gruelling season.

Their side included six members of the British Lions squad to tour South Africa, including captain Martin Johnson, but Stransky's contribution was the main reason former Wallaby coach Bob Dwyer's team emerged on top.
Sheeting rain ruled out much attacking rugby in the first half and both Stransky and Mannix missed their first two penalty attempts as they struggled to master the gusty conditions.

Mannix achieved the rare feat of hitting the crossbar and then a post seconds later when he tried a drop-goal, but he finally put Sale on the scoreboard just before halftime, reducing Leicester's lead to 6-3.
It proved a false dawn as Stransky added a third penalty and Sale wasted late chances to prevent a tryless final, the first since 1982.

Leicester - Niall Malone; Craig Joiner, Will Greenwood, Stuart Potter, Leon Lloyd; Joel Stransky, Austin Healey (Aadel Kardooni, 72nd-76th); Eric Miller, Neil Back, John Wells (Dean Richards, 68th), Matt Poole, Martin Johnson (captain), Darren Garforth, Richard Cockerill, Graham Rowntree.

Sale - Jim Mallinder (captain); David Rees, Jos Baxendell, Adrian Hadley, Tom Beim; Simon Mannix, Dewi Morris; John Mitchell, Dylan O'Grady, Neil Ashurst, Dave Baldwin, Dave Erskine, Andrew Smith, Steve Diamond, Phil Winstanley.
